title: Voy A Versus Intento
voice_notes: Warm, patient teacher. One voice. Brian v3. English prompts use language_code en; Spanish reveals use language_code es. Avoid Language Transfer branding.

segments.say: Two English sentences both use the word to. Spanish does not treat them the same.
Voy means I am going. Going is movement.
When going points to another action, Spanish uses voy a.
See them is verlos: ver plus los.
Say: I am going to see them.
segments.word: I am going to see them

segments.say: Now compare that with intento. Intento means I am trying.
Trying is not movement. So go straight to the next verb.
Say: I am trying to see them.
segments.word: I am trying to see them

segments.say: So the question is simple: is there movement?
If yes, use a. If no, go straight to the verb.
Now say: I am going to try to see them.
segments.word: I am going to try to see them

segments.say: Good. The a came from going, not from trying.

caption: Spanish uses a after movement: voy a verlos. But intento is not movement: intento verlos.
